title: Searching for a principal-prime anchor conserved by the xi support flow
question: can an independent principal-prime or completed-logarithmic-derivative conservation law force the horizontal-residue variation to vanish?

verdict.conclusion: The full half-plane target can be reduced to one absolutely convergent Euler anchor at s=2. For the transported completed divisor, d_t[xi_t'/xi_t(2)] is strictly positive for every off-line quartet and is termwise comparable to minus the horizontal-residue variation. Thus conservation of this one scalar would force RH and zero residue variation. The scalar has an exact principal-prime formula, but the transported divisor has no independently derived Euler product tying it to the same fixed von Mangoldt moment for t>0. The proposed conservation law therefore remains unproved; RH remains open.

eulerAnchor.defectConsequence: the defect is nonnegative and vanishes exactly under RH

quartetAnchorVariation.signAtTwo: strictly positive at w=3/2 for every off-line nontrivial quartet because eta^2<1/4 and gamma^2>199

coerciveResidueComparison.statement: 1.4269*(-partial_t R_hor) <= partial_t[xi_t'/xi_t(2)] <= 1.5196*(-partial_t R_hor), termwise and hence after summation
coerciveResidueComparison.consequence: zero variation of the s=2 completed logarithmic derivative is equivalent to zero horizontal-residue variation and to RH

onePointEquivalence.statement: RH iff partial_t[xi_t'/xi_t(2)] at t=0 is zero iff partial_t R_hor at t=0 is zero
onePointEquivalence.forward: under RH every eta is zero, so both variations vanish
onePointEquivalence.reverse: each off-line quartet contributes strictly positively at s=2 and strictly negatively to R_hor
onePointEquivalence.gain: an open-half-plane conservation law is unnecessary; one absolutely convergent principal-prime moment would suffice

conservationAudit.candidate: static principal von Mangoldt moment at s=2
conservationAudit.result: sum Lambda(n)/n^2 is fixed, but xi_t'/xi_t(2) equals its completed value only at t=0; no Euler product for the transported divisor is derived

conservationAudit.candidate: same Euler product for every t
conservationAudit.result: this would conserve the anchor, but Euler-product uniqueness would already make xi_t=xi; the premise is the stationarity theorem in arithmetic form
the quartet contribution is even in eta, so reflected partners add rather than cancel
multiplying xi_t by a scalar does not change xi_t'/xi_t and cannot affect the anchor variation
Mobius inversion recovers Lambda from the all-integer ledger but supplies no t-evolution intertwining that ledger with the horizontally transported divisor
it derives dot eta=-eta but does not preserve the Euler anchor; off-line support makes the anchor strictly increase

missingTheorem.minimalForm: prove independently that the transported divisor obeys xi_t'/xi_t(2)=3/2-(EulerGamma+log pi)/2-sum Lambda(n)/n^2 for t near zero
missingTheorem.whyNotYetProved: the right side is the fixed principal ledger, whereas xi_t is an auxiliary canonical product with moved zeros; identifying them for t>0 is exactly the missing same-xi compatibility
missingTheorem.status: the target is reduced from all-scale half-plane stationarity to one scalar, but not established

status: no independent conservation law was proved; RH remains open
